blocks.html:
Welcome to OneAccord. This training shows you how we use Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Ninety.io. Whether you've used these tools for years or never, the goal is the same: everyone uses them the same way.

There are seven short lessons. Each one has a few teaching sections, a knowledge check, and in some lessons a scenario that your coach grades (3 of 4 points passes).

Why we standardize

  • Less noise. Internal email chains bury the work that matters. Sorting conversations into the right place keeps your attention on clients and projects.
  • Searchable history. Decisions, discussions and files live in one logical place, so you, your team and future colleagues can find what happened and why.
  • Room to grow. A consistent approach keeps collaboration reliable as we add people, teams and projects.

Intended use

Every tool has a best purpose. Your first job as a new team member is to use each tool for that purpose, even if you did it differently at your last company. That's how you help the whole firm run more smoothly from day one.

Where does my message go?

ChannelUse it forDon't use it for
Outlook emailExternal parties (clients, vendors, partners); anything that needs a formal record or paper trail; formal decisions; firm-wide announcements that need acknowledgmentInternal project coordination, quick internal questions
Teams channel postInternal group work, project discussion, day-to-day decisions, sharing files and linksClient communication, firm-wide announcements
Teams private chatFast, informal questions to one or two peopleProject collaboration and decisions
Ninety.io HeadlineAnything the whole team should see or align on at the next all-team meeting: wins, issues, firm-level updatesUrgent same-day items, one-on-one conversations
SharePoint (the OneAccord Hub)Official reference material you read: policies, resources, trainingAnything that needs a response or decision
Quick test. Ask: Does this need a record, a response, or a meeting?
A record, or it goes outside the firm: Email. A quick internal response: Teams. The team's attention at the meeting: Ninety.io Headline. Just reference material: SharePoint.

blocks.prompt: You need to send a client your revised proposal. Where does it go?
options: A Teams channel post
Outlook email, because the client is outside OneAccord
A Teams private chat
A Ninety.io Headline
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. External parties always get email.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Clients are outside OneAccord, so this goes by Outlook email.

blocks.prompt: You want a teammate's quick opinion on a one-line subject line. What's the best fit?
options: A Teams private chat, because it's quick, informal and involves one or two people
A formal email to the whole team
A new channel post with a long subject line
A Ninety.io Headline
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Exactly. Private chat is for fast, informal questions.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: A quick question to one or two people belongs in a private chat.

blocks.prompt: A project team of five is deciding next week's task split. Where should that discussion happen?
options: In a private chat between two of them
In a long reply-all email chain
In a post in the project's Teams channel
In a Ninety.io Headline
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Channel posts make a permanent, searchable record the whole team can see.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Internal group work belongs in a channel post, where the whole team and future teammates can find it.

blocks.prompt: You closed a great deal and want the team to recognize it. What's the best channel?
options: An email to the whole firm
A private chat with your manager
The OneAccord Hub
A Ninety.io Headline, so it comes up at the all-team meeting
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Wins go in a Ninety.io Headline for the all-team meeting.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Wins are shared as a Ninety.io Headline so the whole team sees them at the all-team meeting.

blocks.prompt: You need the latest approved travel policy. Where do you look?
options: Ask in a private chat
Search your old emails
The OneAccord Hub on SharePoint
Your local Documents folder
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. The Hub is the read-only home for official policies.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: The OneAccord Hub is the single source of truth for approved policies.
